paper.title: Deep Learning for Risky Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Event Prediction in Hypertensive Patients
paper.claim: The reference task classifies hypertensive patients by whether an adjudicated cardiovascular or cerebrovascular event occurs during a 12-month follow-up.
paper.population: Hypertensive patients aged 55 and older from one Naples center; 17 of 139 experienced an adjudicated event during 12-month follow-up.
paper.referenceStandard: Twelve-month follow-up with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events adjudicated from clinical records, patient history, and the reference general practitioner.
paper.relationEvidence: The repository cites the exact paper and is maintained by a named paper coauthor at the pinned revision.

compatibility.window: A low-noise five-minute segment selected from a 24-hour Holter recording.
compatibility.preprocessing: Kubios Premium 3.4.1 beat detection and artifact correction followed by the paper's exact feature extraction, scaling, and frozen model.
mismatches: The current Brainstem resting R-R contract does not reproduce all 64 exact Kubios features.
The fitted source scaler and paired public test labels are unavailable.
The source evaluator reports incorrect AUC and sensitivity/specificity calculations.
Brainstem has no matching adjudicated hypertensive 55+ outcome cohort.

cohort.output: Withheld until corrected public reproduction and protected matching-population validation support an aggregate research result.

personal.output: Withheld; no cardiovascular-event label, probability, risk score, or proxy may be returned from this candidate.
